title: Canonical Model and Value Object Pattern
purpose: Demonstrate a Model that wraps a DB row with computed properties and an immutable Value Object for compound domain concepts. Models have zero framework dependencies.
context: A ResourceCollection value object that represents a set of resources (wood, stone, food) and a PlayerResources Model that wraps the player's resource DB row. The Manager returns these to callers instead of raw arrays.
before: $resources = ['wood' => 3, 'stone' => 2, 'food' => 1]; if ($resources['wood'] >= 2) { $resources['wood'] -= 2; self::DbQuery("UPDATE player SET resources = '" . json_encode($resources) . "' WHERE player_id = $playerId"); }
after: class ResourceCollection { function __construct(private array $resources) {} function has(string $type, int $qty): bool { return ($this->resources[$type] ?? 0) >= $qty; } function spend(string $type, int $qty): self { $new = $this->resources; $new[$type] = ($new[$type] ?? 0) - $qty; return new self($new); } function toArray(): array { return $this->resources; } } class PlayerResources { function __construct(private DB $db, private int $playerId) {} function load(): ResourceCollection { $row = $this->db->get("SELECT wood, stone, food, gold FROM player_resource WHERE player_id = $this->playerId"); return new ResourceCollection(['wood' => (int)$row['wood'], 'stone' => (int)$row['stone'], 'food' => (int)$row['food'], 'gold' => (int)$row['gold']]); } function save(ResourceCollection $resources): void { $data = $resources->toArray(); $this->db->update("UPDATE player_resource SET wood = $data[wood], stone = $data[stone], food = $data[food], gold = $data[gold] WHERE player_id = $this->playerId"); } }
explanation: ResourceCollection is an immutable value object (ARCH-013). Each operation returns a new instance — the original is unchanged, preventing accidental mutation. PlayerResources is a Model that wraps a DB row (ARCH-011). It has zero framework dependencies — no Game reference, no globals (ARCH-012). The Manager calls PlayerResources::load() which returns a ResourceCollection, and PlayerResources::save() which persists changes. Callers receive typed objects instead of raw arrays, making the code self-documenting and type-safe (ARCH-009).
common_mistakes: Returning raw associative arrays from Manager read methods instead of Models
Making Models depend on the Game framework (Game reference, globals, DB queries in the Model)
Mutating value objects in place instead of returning new instances
Storing compound data as JSON blobs in a single column instead of normalized columns
Using the same object for read and write without a clear save path through the Manager

annotations.reason: Immutable value object. Each operation returns new instance.
has() and spend() are pure — no side effects.
Model encapsulates a DB row with typed accessors.
Zero framework dependencies. No Game, no globals, no notify.
Read method returns Model object, not raw array.
